feeds.title: The Mom Kind
feeds.description: Autism Parenting resource for the modern parent. Alicia Trautwein created this website to help support autistic individuals and their families. She is an Autism Advocate & Motivational Speaker.

feeds.title: The Autism Dad Blog
feeds.description: The real-life story of a family coping not only with autism but multiple, serious physical and emotional health issues. Rob Gorski writes about his life as a single Dad raising 3 autistic kids.

feeds.title: Finding Cooper's Voice
feeds.description: My name is Kate and I am the mama to two wild and crazy boys, Sawyer (age 4) and Cooper (age 6). Cooper has severe, non-verbal autism. As you can imagine, raising a child with a disability has impacted my life in every way possible. I invite you to take a glimpse inside the secret world of Autism. It is sad, funny, scary and heartbreaking. And most of all full of hope and love.

feeds.title: Autism Parenting Magazine
feeds.description: The magazine features the latest news, tips, and advice for parents of children with Asperger's Syndrome, Kanner's Autism, and PDD-NOS. Covers subjects like: behavioral tips, sensory processing issues, mitigating meltdowns, special education needs, and getting access to services.

feeds.title: Stages Learning Blog
feeds.description: Autism resources, lesson plans, treatment options, support, research updates, family support from experts, educators, parents, and therapists. Stages Learning is dedicated to creating quality teaching tools to help educators provide the best learning opportunities for students on the autism spectrum.

feeds.title: The Autism Cafe
feeds.description: The Autism Cafe Blog was founded by Eileen Lamb and shares the ups and downs of raising a severely autistic child while being on the autism. She is the author of All Across The Spectrum, a photographer, and a mom raising two children with health conditions. She aims to spread autism awareness through her blog. Take a walk through her blog and learn more about services, articles, portfolios, photography, and more.

feeds.title: Autism Spectrum News
feeds.description: Autism Spectrum News (ASN), published by the 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization Mental Health News Education, began as a quarterly print publication in 2008. ASN was developed to provide the autism community with a trusted source of evidence-based information and education, the latest in scientific research, clinical treatment best practices, family issues, advocacy, and vital community resources.

feeds.title: 101autism
feeds.description: Welcome to 101 Autism Team, where we share the daily experiences of a family living with autism. This site is a space for families to connect, share stories, and find support. We will be sharing stories from our everyday lives, highlighting the moments of triumph and the challenges we face. We also want to share our experiences with various products that help or hinder our daily lives.

feeds.title: Life After An ABA Classroom
feeds.description: Sandy Moats is a former teacher's Assistant in Autism Support and discusses the lifelong condition of Autism. She offers resources and insights on many services and organizations, such as the Autism Research Institute, which provides checklists for evaluating behavior and illnesses associated with autism.

feeds.title: BlueSprig Blog
feeds.description: At BlueSprig we're on a mission to change the world for children with autism. The families and children we serve are at the heart of everything we do. Our dedicated team of clinically excellent BCBAs, RBTs, BTs, and administrative staff provide the highest standard of care so that you and your child receive the best ABA treatment available. Our goal is to provide the very best and most compassionate ABA therapy services to all children who need it, regardless of their means.

feeds.title: Artfully Autistic
feeds.description: This Publication is for all who are Autistic and for those of our kind. It is for the Neurodivergent, for those on the Spectrum of all Gender Identities, the LGBTQ*, and all others who are justifiably non-conformant to Society's harmful marginalization and Ableist views of us.

feeds.title: Autism Classroom Resources Blog
feeds.description: Christine Reeve shares autism resources and tips for the classroom, homeschooling, and virtual learning. Her goal is to develop strategies and materials to provide meaningful and practical support to teachers and caregivers of individuals with autism spectrum disorder and other related disorders.

feeds.title: Autism Awareness Centre News
feeds.description: Maureen's blog is about current events, resources, and a variety of relevant topics about Autism & Autism Spectrum Disorder (formerly Asperger's). Maureen Bennie created the Autism Awareness Centre in 2003 to address what she saw as a gap in support, information, resources and advocacy for those struggling with autism spectrum disorders.

feeds.title: Dr. Mary Barbera Blog
feeds.description: A blog about practical autism ABA strategies for parents and professionals. Authored by Mary Barbera, a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA-D).

feeds.title: Different Brains » Autism
feeds.description: Different Brains strives to encourage understanding & acceptance of individuals who have variations in brain function and social behaviors known as neurodiversity. Our mission has 3 pillars: To mentor neurodiverse adults in maximizing their potential for employment and independence, To increase awareness of neurodiversity by producing interactive media, To foster the next generation of neurodivergent self-advocates.

feeds.title: Affect Autism Blog
feeds.description: Developmental happens through relationships across a lifetime. Join Daria Brown as she dives into implementing a Floortime approach with neurodivergent individuals and listen to her 'We Chose Play' podcast. Learn how to support your child using the Developmental, Individual differences, Relationship-based (DIR®) model.

feeds.title: HomeSchool Special Needs Tidbits
feeds.description: This website Blog features books that I have purchased, insight and experiences while homeschooling our autistic son. I never thought in my wildest dreams that my degree in social work and minors in Health Care Administration and Psychology would lead me to this, but here I am. I will also do my best to share many resources with more information about how they empower me to be the best teacher that I could be and continue to advocate for all of our son's educational and daily living skills as well.

feeds.title: AU-TI
feeds.description: AU-TI Media for Autism News specializing in providing relevant news snippets, vital journalism, quizzes, celebrity gossip and life hacks.

feeds.title: Teaching Autism Blog
feeds.description: Hi, my name is Nikki, and I'm the face behind Teaching Autism. I have extensive experience working within Special Education, specifically with children diagnosed with Autism. Creating resources that are differentiated and tailored to suit my students is my passion, and I love to make them that extra bit fun too.

feeds.title: Rarer in Girls...My Daughter with Autism
feeds.description: I'm Suzanne, and this blog is about life with my daughter Janey, who is autistic & has an intellectual disability. I do my best to write here about our lives with Janey in an honest way, one that shows both the difficulties & the joys of raising her. I hope by writing to provide support, encouragement, and love to others with a child-like Janey.

feeds.title: Autism Answers with Tsara Shelton
feeds.description: Musings, Shared Family Stories, Book Reviews, and Short Fiction written by Tsara Shelton. Tsara writes stories grown from the fertile and organic thinking soil where autism or parenting come together.

feeds.title: Autism Policy and Politics Blog
feeds.description: John J. Pitney Jr. is the Roy P. Crocker Professor of American Politics at Claremont McKenna College in Claremont, California. He received his B.A. in political science from Union College, where he was co-valedictorian. He earned his Ph.D. in political science at Yale, where he was a National Science Foundation Fellow. He has written a book on the politics of autism policy. Building on this research, this blog offers insights, analysis, and facts about recent events.

feeds.title: Rainbows Are Too Beautiful
feeds.description: The blog is a place for Ann to share her experiences of life with her autistic and neurotypical kids and an opportunity to promote awareness and greater understanding of autism. The blog also provides light on ADHD, hypermobility, SPD, dyspraxia, anxiety and sleep issues.

feeds.title: Learn From Autistics Blog
feeds.description: Covers autism interviews, parenting tips, and autism news. Learn from Autistics provides practical solutions for parents and families of children and young adults on the autism spectrum.

feeds.title: The Autism Helper Blog
feeds.description: The Autism Helper, Inc. empowers Autism support networks with resources and tools for success. Their blog, podcast, and training videos offer accessible strategies. Through CE Courses and live events, they deliver comprehensive training. Their focus on positive behaviour change, high expectations, and data-driven decisions adds value to educators, parents, clinicians, and administrators.

feeds.title: AwesomismMom Blog
feeds.description: We're working to raise Autism Awareness, Acceptance, and Activism. Hi! My name is Lynne, also known as AwesomismMom! We're working to help spread our positive message, 'Turning Autism into Awesomism!'

feeds.title: Madison House Autism Foundation Blog
feeds.description: MHAF provides hope, guidance and effective solutions to autistic adults and their families.

feeds.title: Naturally Recovering Autism Blog
feeds.description: My name is Karen Thomas and I have spent over thirty years in the field of holistic health. My passion for helping other moms naturally recover their children came from my own child's diagnosis on the autism spectrum. My holistic background and knowledge of the brain assured me that my own child could and would recover if given the right support. Naturally Recovering Autism is the result of over twelve years of research, expense, trial, and error to discover what really works to recover a child from autism, naturally.

feeds.title: Mitchell's Life with Autism
feeds.description: My name is Mitchell and I am an autistic teen. I want to share my life with the world in hopes that I can bring awareness of what it is like to live with autism. I believe spelling as a form of communication is not well understood and I hope to bring awareness to this lifestyle and change that for autistic people everywhere. I am on the move a lot because it helps me concentrate and apply myself.

feeds.title: The Autistic Me
feeds.description: The Autistic Me features reflections on daily life with autism from the perspective of a university professor diagnosed with high-functioning autism. Frank and unvarnished, these are one autistic's experiences.

feeds.title: Cultivate BHE Blog
feeds.description: Cultivate provides ABA therapy services in Central Texas , serving children with autism and other developmental disabilities . We serve children starting in their early intervention programs, through their high school years. Through our Applied Behavior

feeds.title: Think Psych Blog
feeds.description: Central NJ provider of comprehensive behavior analysis services including assessment, consultation, and training.

feeds.title: The Ringmasters Tale
feeds.description: I'm Helen: Autism advocate, psychotherapist, charity founder, author, public speaker and mum to four amazing children on the autism spectrum. The purpose of my writing is to offer help and advice to anyone who needs it, and to be that reassuring voice I so needed to hear all those years ago when my children were small and my world was filled with endless chaos and universal disapproval.

feeds.title: ChevsLife
feeds.description: Living & Parenting with Intent - Unmasking the Journey to Optimism and autism. Chivone is a single parent in the journey of motherhood.

feeds.title: Learn Play Thrive Blog
feeds.description: I'm Meg Proctor, an occupational therapist, autism specialist, and feeding therapist. I love helping children with autism and other disabilities participate more fully in their lives. But even more, I love helping parents learn some practical, realistic things to try out during their daily routines. Read our blog to find Up-to-date strategies from an occupational therapist and autism specialist to help kids with autism thrive in every day life.

feeds.title: Raising My Little Superheroes
feeds.description: Join us on our journey through life with Autism.

feeds.title: A Side of Gold Fish
feeds.description: Life experiences, advice, tips and tricks, and nonsense from a working Autism mom wanting to make the world a kinder, wiser place for her son

feeds.title: My Autistic Heart
feeds.description: Life from the perspective of a 31 year old autistic business owner with an autistic family. My news and views on my autistic life and family.Due to autism being a spectrum and subjective, please take my views as personal accounts and not fact for every autistic person. We're all different and equally wonderful in our uniqueness. Thanks!

feeds.title: Thriving Wellness Center Blog
feeds.description: Covers ADHD, autism and a variety of topics including trauma, human behavior, and advanced clinical topics.

feeds.title: Autism Adventures Abroad
feeds.description: My name is Alex Stratikis, founder of 'Autism Adventures Abroad'.Come with me on my journeys and learn more about the world through the autistic lens. I know I cannot speak for everyone who has autism, we are as individual as every other person on this planet but, I hope whoever you are, you find my posts informative and enjoyable, and you get to know me and my autistic perspective of this amazing world we live in.

feeds.title: The Real Spectrum Blog
feeds.description: I'm Gabriele. I have recently become very interested in the neuroscience of Autism since my younger brother was diagnosed with ASD about 2 years ago. Seeing how profoundly ASD has impacted his life as well as my family's life, I am passionate about gaining a stronger understanding of the science behind the disorder as well as advocating for autism awareness in my school and community.

feeds.title: Teach Love Autism Blog
feeds.description: I'm Jenn. I am a special education and elementary education teacher with 14 years of teaching experience. I love helping teachers, students, and their families to gain the skills they need to be more independent! I decided to start a blog to keep a public diary of my life as a teacher in an autistic support classroom with middle schoolers.

feeds.title: Hi Blog! I'm Dad.
feeds.description: I'm James Guttman, father of two children. One six year old (non verbal) and one nine year old (nonstop verbal). My mission is to share stories about his family, understanding autism, life after a quintuple bypass at 35, and overall topics that he feels might resonate with others.

feeds.title: The Art of Autism
feeds.description: The Art of Autism empowers autistic people and their families through the Arts which includes visual arts, music, blogging, poetry, dance, and other art forms.

feeds.title: The Autism Daddy
feeds.description: I'm a 47-year-old neurotypical dad with a 14-year-old sonwith severe, non-verbal autism and now also with Epilepsy. I show what being an autistic dad is really like, the good & the bad, the pee & the poop.

feeds.title: By Jessica Watson
feeds.description: Hi, I'm Jessica, a 40-something mom to five, four in my arms and one in my heart. On any given day you will find me taxi-ing a teenager, debating with my preteens, and thanking God that my youngest isn't growing up as fast as the rest of them all the while, looking for the closest Starbucks drive-thru in Southeast Michigan.

feeds.title: Autism with A Side of Fries
feeds.description: Living the life with a son on the spectrum who proves that a side of fries makes anything better.

feeds.title: Neuro Clastic
feeds.description: Content about autism by autistic and neurodivergent people. Neuro Clastic is a collective of actually autistic writers and artists advocating for autistic representation and human rights.

feeds.title: The Neurodiversity Trailblazer
feeds.description: A blog about autism awareness and disability rights. Authored by Sarah Ramos, a female activist, and early childhood educator.

feeds.title: The Autistic Traveler Blog
feeds.description: The Autistic Traveler is for late-identified autistic adults who are new or seasoned travelers, whether that means taking the local bus downtown or wandering the five continents. I chronicle my travels with the hope that one autistic person's experiences can offer you useful insights and tools.

feeds.title: Autism Info
feeds.description: Autism Info provides a forum for families who are battling with Autism to get information and resources easily in one place. Get help and help others to win over Autism! Autism, also known as Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), is a neurodevelopmental disorder that affects how individuals perceive and interact with the world around them.

feeds.title: Autism Products Blog
feeds.description: Hi. I'm Kelly. I created this site so that you don't have to search as hard as I did to find products for my child. Ever since my son Jack was diagnosed, I have been on the lookout for products to help with his sensory needs. I hope that you not only find what you need but find my site a little comforting in that you are not the only one searching for these products.

feeds.title: Aviva Seigler
feeds.description: Aviva Seigler is the executive director at Autistic Inclusive Meets the USA and a website editor for Autistic Inclusive Meets. She is a writer, an activist, and an advocate. Her hope is to bridge the gap between allies and autistics while fighting the pseudoscience that threatens all people, not just autistics.

feeds.title: Undercover Autism
feeds.description: Emma is one of the directors of Autism Wellbeing CIC, a non-profit organization working alongside people to change the way autism is perceived. This blog contains personal insights and the occasional professional reflection. Her current Ph.D. research explores perceptions of autism within community mental health services.

feeds.title: Positive Autism Blog
feeds.description: Features articles that have to do exclusively with Autism and related topics. Authored by Dr. A M Reddy, a renowned Homeopathic physician and the principal founder & director of Dr.Positive Health Sciences.

feeds.title: Big Abilities Blog
feeds.description: Amy is a former educator of 20 years. She has four children ranging in age from 3-31. In addition to being a mother, she enjoys watching sports and travel. She started Big Abilities to be an advocate for children with developmental disabilities and to encourage families to not only accept their child for who they are but to embrace them.

feeds.title: Go Team Kate
feeds.description: A blog about a family's autism triumphs and struggles. Following a little girl's autism diagnosis and beyond.

feeds.title: Speaking of Autism…
feeds.description: An autistic speaks about living with autism. Quincy Hansen is an autistic 17-year-old and is the one who writes this blog. This blog was started as a platform to reach a wider audience with an autistic take on autism, neurodiversity, and acceptance. Quincy hopes that this blog will help people get a better idea about how he and other autistic people process the world and provide a place for other autistic people to read and relate.

feeds.title: The Musical Autist Blog
feeds.description: Our mission is to provide equal rights to the fine arts and to create platforms for self advocacy, by giving credentialed music therapists the tools and resources they need to facilitate Sensory Friendly Concerts in their own local communities.

feeds.title: Side by Side Therapy Blog
feeds.description: Side by Side Therapy offers behaviour analytic services to children with Autism Spectrum Disorder and other special needs.

feeds.title: Jewel Autism Centre
feeds.description: We are one of the best autism centre providing Autism Treatment in India, Kerala. We also provide Occupational Therapy, Speech Therapy & Behavioural Therapy.

feeds.title: Autism in Our Nest
feeds.description: Robyn Coupe has two children on the autism spectrum and writes about her experiences on the blog, Autism in Our Nest. From exploring therapy for her children to experiencing isolation as a parent, Robyn shares a personal glimpse of her family's journey with autism.

feeds.title: In the Loop About Neurodiversity
feeds.description: Welcome, and thank you for stopping by! My name is Cassandra Crosman, and I am the creator of 'In the Loop About Neurodiversity.' I am a 23 year old neurodivergent college student who has studied various subjects in humanities and social science such as communication studies, philosophy, and political science. In the Loop About Neurodiversity is a platform that seeks to educate others on what neurodiversity is and how to better serve neurodiverse people.

feeds.title: Squidalicious
feeds.description: Formerly known as The Adventures of Leelo and His Potty-Mouthed Mom. Geekery, parenting, autism, all that.

feeds.title: Autism Plus More Blog
feeds.description: Welcome to my blog. This blog will primarily focus on Autism, Sensory Processing Disorder, and Parents/Caregivers. The journey is individualized but I am going to share my son's journey along with personal challenges I've overcome to maintain my health to be able to be the best parent and caregiver he has.

feeds.title: Best Practice Autism
feeds.description: Dr. Lee A. Wilkinson is author of the award-winning book, A Best Practice Guide to Assessment and Intervention for Autism and Asperger Syndrome in Schools.

feeds.title: One Autism Mom's Notes
feeds.description: One Autism Mom's Notes is a weekly blog that provides a mother's reflections on raising a child with autism.

feeds.title: A diary of a mom
feeds.description: A blog by Jess, a mother, intersectional advocate, believer in the power of community.

feeds.title: Autism Journey Blog
feeds.description: Welcome to Autism Journey Autism Journey is home for parents of children with an autism spectrum disorder. We provide personal stories and experiences about raising a child with an ASD, as well as quality information, resources and more.

feeds.title: Indie Autism
feeds.description: A Mingling of Behavior Science and Practical Life. Hi, I'm Elena! Mom, wife, sister, aunt & friend. Board Certified Assistant Behavior Analyst. Mission: to support families juggling life with their autistic child's therapy needs. All families welcome!

feeds.title: Faith, Hope, and Love...With Autism
feeds.description: Faith, Hope, and Love...With Autism is a blog by Lisa Reyes who shares her experience of raising a kid with autism and his journey towards autism recovery.

feeds.title: Sarah Nannery Blog
feeds.description: Sarah Nannery's Blog, Quirky & Bright, covering her life experiences as a professional woman and mother with Autism.

feeds.title: Our Chaos
feeds.description: Welcome to Our Chaos! We're just a typical blog about our atypical family with a teen living with autism, a stay at home dad, and a working mom!

feeds.title: Dyslexic and Autistic? Yep,That's me!
feeds.description: Living Life with Dyslexia and Autism.

feeds.title: Rainbows and Lighthouses
feeds.description: Sharing my experiences trying to be a Lighthouse for my little Rainbow. My amazing daughter was diagnosed with Autism in March 2017. Join us on our journey.

feeds.title: Not Weird Just Autistic
feeds.description: J.R. Reed is an autism self-advocate who preaches Neurodiversity and does it all from a log cabin in the Missouri Ozarks. He blogs speaks and writes on a wide variety of topics affecting those with developmental disabilities, both adults and children. He's spoken to groups, companies, and at the Missouri State Capitol.

feeds.title: Autism Learning Felt Blog
feeds.description: Autism blog raising a child with autism family support website.

feeds.title: A slice of Autism
feeds.description: A slice of family life living with Autism.

feeds.title: Spectroomz
feeds.description: Spectroomz is an autism employment blog focusing on jobs for autistic people and people with Aspergers

feeds.title: Ausome Girls
feeds.description: A place to gather and share. Something I've noticed since realizing I'm autistic is the insight I can share with all NT parents.

feeds.title: Atypical Familia
feeds.description: Atypical Familia (formerly Autismwonderland) is a personal blog that focuses on autism parenting, family travel, working mom life & more.

feeds.title: Finding My Kid
feeds.description: Finding My Kid is a blog by a parent of a kid with autism. In this blog, you will see how Martin is overcoming autism with his determination and will and with the support of his parents.

feeds.title: From an Autistic Point of View
feeds.description: This blog was founded to show people that there is more than one type of Autism, and is a look into the life of a young woman with high functioning autism. Not all are the super smart intellectuals that you see on various specials getting hired by places such as IBM, Microsoft, Google, and the like. Others are more like me, Artsy Autistics. As founder of this blog, it is my job to show you what living as an Artsy Autistic is like, both the good and the bad sides.

feeds.title: Autistic & Unapologetic
feeds.description: Autistic & Unapologetic is an autism site that helps autistic people and their families to understand and embrace autism through fun and fascinating articles.

feeds.title: Susan Senator Blog
feeds.description: Helpful and Interesting Autism Information. My own articles, essays, opeds, blog posts, as well as others' advocacy news and updates.

feeds.title: Autistic Hoya
feeds.description: A blog by Lydia X. Z. Brown. Lydia X. Z. Brown (Autistic Hoya) is a gender/queer and transracially/transnationally adopted east asian autistic activist, writer, and speaker whose work has largely focused on violence against multiply-marginalized disabled people, especially institutionalization, incarceration, and policing.

feeds.title: Autistic Not Weird
feeds.description: Articles and insight about autism from Chris Bonnello, an autistic author, advocate, speaker, and former teacher.

feeds.title: Look Me In The Eye
feeds.description: Follow the personal journey through autism with the author John Elder Robison. Official blog of NYT bestselling author, photographer, educator, neurodiversity advocate and automobile aficionado John Elder Robison.

feeds.title: Thinking Person's Guide to Autism
feeds.description: Daily autism news, resources, & discussions from autistic people, professionals, and parents. The Thinking Person's Guide to Autism is a small team of volunteers who curate information and make it usable as a resource for others.

feeds.title: EMPOWERED NEUROFAMILIES Blog
feeds.description: Kaylene George is an autistic self-advocate, author, and mother of five, including one autistic child. She realized her own autism as an adult shortly after her son received his initial diagnosis. Suddenly the parts of her that seemed so 'weird' to society had an answer. Since then, Kaylene has passionately shared her experiences with autism from both sides of the great divide between parents and autistic self-advocates.

feeds.title: GreaterGood Blog
feeds.description: Read the latest Autism stories, research, inspiration, technology, and nutrition. The Autism Site was born out of the desire to spread the word about the growing number of children and families who are coping with the challenge of autism and to provide a way for everyone to help.

feeds.title: Prayatna Blog
feeds.description: Read blog articles enriched with expert tips, techniques & strategies for helping your child to achieve their full potential. Prayatna is a front-runner establishment in the area, devoted to changing the lives of autistic children reliant on evidence-based therapies and compassionate counseling.

feeds.title: Embrace Autism Blog
feeds.description: Quality autism information can help us make sense of our lives, it can help us discover who we are and the amazing potential we have, and it can help us acknowledge the beauty and splendor in ourselves and each other. And of course, Embrace Autism is also a vessel to share our own interest in autism, and our explorations in the research literature. Because we greatly enjoy the learning process, are excited to share our findings and get invigorated by the empowering effect it has on autistic people like us.

feeds.title: Autisable Blog
feeds.description: Bringing together the Autism Community to connect, share and discuss all things Autism.

feeds.title: Age of Autism
feeds.description: Daily insights into the autism epidemic. Age of Autism is a non-profit organization, their mission is to share information with families facing the daily challenges & joys that surround autism.

feeds.title: The Real Michael Tanzer
feeds.description: Michael Tanzer shares his Point of View (POV) on Life with Autism and hopes that the reader will gain a better understanding of individuals with ASD. Michael is an Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Advocator and has written several articles for a Canadian magazine called Autism Matters.

feeds.title: Autism Society
feeds.description: Cover latest Autism information regarding treatment, education, research, and advocacy. The Autism Society is a network of members and supporters dedicated to improving the lives of people affected by autism.

feeds.title: Association for Autism and Neurodiversity (AANE)
feeds.description: AANE helps Autistic and similarly Neurodivergent people build meaningful, connected lives. We provide individuals, families, and professionals with education, community, and support in an inclusive atmosphere of validation and respect.

feeds.title: Autism Speaks Blog
feeds.description: Autism Speaks is dedicated to creating an inclusive world for all individuals with autism throughout their lifespan. In response to the pressing needs of the 1 in 36 children and 1 in 45 adults with autism in the U.S. today, the nonprofit provides resources and tools for autistic individuals of all ages and levels of support from early diagnosis & intervention, to transition to adulthood, to aging with autism, and beyond...
